notes: Prompts mix triggering tests (would a real CodeLens phrasing pull this skill?) and output-quality tests (does the output follow the locked Java 21 conventions: virtual threads, records, sealed adapter, exhaustive switch, no preview APIs). Assertions are objectively checkable.

evals.prompt: In the CodeLens backend, write the component that reviews every diff chunk of a PR concurrently. One chunk failing (a timeout or bad LLM output) must not lose the comments from the other chunks.
evals.expected_output: A service using Executors.newVirtualThreadPerTaskExecutor(), submitting one task per chunk, joining each Future with a per-future try/catch so failures are isolated. No fixed-size pool, no preview APIs.

assertions.text: Catches per-future exceptions so one chunk failure does not abort the others
Does NOT use a fixed-size thread pool (newFixedThreadPool / Executors.newFixedThreadPool)
Does NOT use StructuredTaskScope or any --enable-preview API

evals.prompt: Define the data types the review pipeline streams: the per-token fragment pushed over WebSocket and the completed, validated comment. Severity is critical/warning/suggestion.
evals.expected_output: Java records (not POJOs) for the token and comment, a Severity enum, and a compact constructor validating confidence in [0,1].

assertions.text: Declares the DTOs as record types, not classes with getters/setters
Defines an enum Severity with CRITICAL, WARNING, SUGGESTION
Validates confidence range in a compact constructor

evals.prompt: Set up the LLM provider in CodeLens so we can switch between a GPT-5 provider and a Claude provider without recompiling, and so the compiler forces us to handle every provider in any dispatch logic.
evals.expected_output: A sealed interface LlmReviewProvider permitting the concrete providers, with a providerId() method and Flux<ReviewToken> streamReview(...); selection driven by config; exhaustive switch examples.

assertions.text: Declares a sealed interface with a permits clause listing the providers
Provider is selected from configuration, not hardcoded in a service
Uses an exhaustive switch over the sealed type with no default branch

evals.prompt: Add the helper that turns a review comment's severity into a labeled, emoji-prefixed string for the GitHub summary.
evals.expected_output: A switch pattern-matching expression over the Severity enum, exhaustive (no default needed).

assertions.text: Uses a switch expression over Severity
Switch is exhaustive over the enum constants with no default branch

evals.prompt: Write an integration test proving CodeLens cannot create two review sessions for the same PR and the same commit SHA.
evals.expected_output: A TestContainers test using postgres:16-alpine wired via @DynamicPropertySource, asserting the second save of the same (pr_id, head_sha) throws DataIntegrityViolationException.

assertions.text: Uses TestContainers with a postgres:16 image, not an embedded/in-memory DB
Asserts a DataIntegrityViolationException (or constraint violation) on the duplicate (pr_id, head_sha)

evals.prompt: For the repo-aware context feature, fetch the diff, the changed function's callers, and its test files in parallel — but if any of the three fails, abandon the whole context and surface the error.
evals.expected_output: Virtual-thread executor with three Futures; on failure of any, cancel(true) the others and throw. Explicitly NOT StructuredTaskScope (preview).

assertions.text: Runs the three fetches on a virtual-thread executor
On any failure, cancels the sibling futures before throwing (fail-together)
